sources.citation: Z'graggen, John A. 1969. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Madang District, New Guinea. PhD thesis, Australian National University.
sources.note: Sepa appears only in cognate-percentage tables. General note on transcription (pp. 13-14): 'The marking of stress has been omitted, since the stress patterning has not been well established yet.' Nothing Sepa-specific.

States that besides Anthropos articles he 'verfasste eine Grammatik und Wörterbücher der Lokalsprachen' (wrote a grammar and dictionaries of the local languages) — apparently unpublished manuscripts; dates the WZKM Sepa texts to vol. 38 (1931), pp. 249-262.

sources.note: Lists no grammar, grammar sketch, phonology or dictionary for Sepa; the seven hh.bib entries coded [spe] are Ross 1988, Z'graggen 1968/1969/1975, Laycock 1973/1976 (overview/comparative/wordlist) and Schebesta 1932 (text). Subclassification refs Lichtenberk 1983, Ross 1988; comment Z'graggen 1969:189.

sources.note: Sepa appears only as a Schouten-chain data language (wordlists, sound correspondences). The only stress remarks (example 3.115 and discussion) concern Ali and Tumleo verb stress alternations; nothing on Sepa stress.

sources.note: Sepa entry: 'All data from Z'graggen (1971). According to Z'graggen, Sepa shares 72% cognates with Manam, and could therefore be regarded as a dialect of it; however, indigenous opinion is firm that it should be regarded as a separate language'. No phonology, no stress.
